answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to forge a costly reputation bond: before an agent earns, it must stake funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Like a willow bending in a canyon wind, the system flexes around honest mistakes but snaps back hard on abuse, keeping verification cheap for real agents while attackers pay linearly for every clone they create.
